title: First Signal for Ilse
text:
Up on the roof, the neon hums below,
Vega turns the dial and the city answers slow.
I carry her the voices from the swap-hour air,
a baker's laugh, a tram bell, someone calling 'where?'
We lay them down like beads on a string,
and Ilse's words go in between each thing.
It's clumsy, I know, the rhythm drags a bit,
but Vega's light comes on, so I'll keep it.

title: Waiting Under the Cloud
text:
I sit on the roof and wait for Vega.
The cloud is low and grey above the city.
The neon blinks red, then blue, then red.
I do not know how long she will take.
I hold the card and try to make the words fit.
The words do not fit well yet.
But the cloud is soft, and I am still waiting.

title: Drizzle on the Roof
text:
The drizzle falls on the roof tonight,
the neon buzzes pink and white.
I wait for Vega, the nine o'clock hour,
and the sky stays open, a patient flower.
The Chariklo question sits in my hand,
I ask it once, then let it stand.
The rain runs down like little wires,
and I am waiting, warm with desires.

title: Waiting for the Sky
text:
The drizzle is small on my hands.
Vega sits beside me, quiet and close.
The sky is still shut like a lid.
I count the drops on the roof,
one, two, then I lose the count.
A notch on both sides, Vega says,
maybe, maybe not. We will see.
I wait, and the sky waits too.

title: Cloud Above the Tin
text:
A cloud sits low above the tin.
Vega dozes, her light turned thin.
I hold my pencil, not quite sure,
and write the cloud, small and pure.
The neon hums its pink and blue.
I wait for moths. I think they're due.
The Chariklo red can wait for her.
We'll check it fresh, not in a blur.

title: The Kettle on the Late Desk
text:
The kettle clicks and starts to sing.
Dario's radio hums along.
I hold my cup, the steam goes up,
and the rooftop lights are soft and small.
Vega's asleep, her light turned low.
I think of rings I cannot see.
The kettle hums, then goes quiet,
and I still have the warm to hold.
